items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: He mentioned two guys. Conrad Gozzo, who is a lead trumpet player, and Irv Cottler...

ctx.x: What prompted you to move from one coast to the other?

Well I got burned out to start with. I was married to a lady and we got divorced. Because I met her in California and we got married. I was 24, she was about 18. I moved to California, and I’d leave her here. I lived in New York, I’d leave her here, and I’d go on the road for eight, nine months at a time. And we had no life. I mean I was bad. I was really bad in those days. And so we got divorced and about six months later we started talking again, you know, saying if I would stay home more maybe we could work it…

Frank Sinatra for 20 years. “Are you kidding? Forget about it. Goodbye.” He hung up on me. I got a call about three days later. And then he said, “Listen, I’m going to put you on staff.” And I knew the reason why. The reason why was because I used to do these television — like Dinah Shore Show — as a guest. Now they don’t have to pay me because they can put me on these shows. So he was going to put me on. So in the long run NBC would save money.
